title: Witness coupons from the Ilyr optical-coating run
public_context: Optical-coating production is often checked with witness coupons and reference standards. Measured reflectance can vary with coating thickness, instrument calibration, sample position, and surface handling. A mismatch between instruments needs careful interpretation when calibration artifacts or measurement geometry differ. Any comparison may need a repeat measurement.
source_text:
The Ilyr laboratory deposited a pale-green interference coating on twelve glass witness coupons during one vacuum run. Six coupons sat near the center of the rotating carrier and six near its outer ring. A ceramic reference plate was measured before the run and again after the chamber cooled; its certificate lists a reflectance band from 520 to 610 nanometres. The plate was stored in a rigid sleeve, but the sleeve was found open after the post-run measurement.

A bench spectrometer measured the center coupons within the expected reflectance band. Two outer-ring coupons showed a shallow dip near 575 nanometres, while the other four did not. The operator repeated those two measurements after rotating each coupon by a quarter turn; the dip remained, although its depth changed slightly. The lab record reports the feature as repeatable on those coupons, not as a confirmed coating defect.

A second instrument at the conservator's room showed a broader dip on all twelve coupons. That instrument had been transported the previous afternoon, and its calibration check used a different ceramic tile whose certificate covered 540 to 640 nanometres. The memorandum notes that the two certificates overlap only partly. No shared reference coupon was measured on both instruments during the same session, so the cross-instrument difference cannot be assigned to the coating alone.

The team did not use the open sleeve as proof that the reference plate had been contaminated. The plate showed no visible mark, and the lab had no surface-residue assay for it. Nor did the authors infer coating thickness directly from dip depth; the run lacked a same-glass thickness series. A brief microscope check found faint handling arcs on one outer coupon, but those arcs did not align with the two repeated dips.

The memorandum recommends a same-session transfer check using one reference artifact and a rotation jig before the next run. It also asks that the reference plate sleeve be sealed and logged at each handoff. The authors leave open whether the broader room-instrument feature reflects calibration, transport, or measurement geometry. They do not recommend changing the coating recipe from this set of measurements, and the observed optical feature has not been linked to performance in a finished sensor.
authoring_note: The evidence structure distinguishes repeatable coupon features from a cross-instrument mismatch whose reference bands and measurement sessions do not align.

supported_claims.claim: Twelve pale-green coated glass coupons were positioned in center and outer carrier groups.
evidence: The Ilyr laboratory deposited a pale-green interference coating on twelve glass witness coupons during one vacuum run. Six coupons sat near the center of the rotating carrier and six near its outer ring.

supported_claims.claim: Two outer coupons showed a shallow reflectance dip near 575 nanometres that persisted under rotation with a small depth change.
evidence: Two outer-ring coupons showed a shallow dip near 575 nanometres, while the other four did not. The operator repeated those two measurements after rotating each coupon by a quarter turn; the dip remained, although its depth changed slightly.

supported_claims.claim: The second instrument showed a broader dip on all coupons and had been transported the previous afternoon.
evidence: A second instrument at the conservator's room showed a broader dip on all twelve coupons.
That instrument had been transported the previous afternoon, and its calibration check used a different ceramic tile whose certificate covered 540 to 640 nanometres.

supported_claims.claim: The two reference certificates overlapped only partly and there was no same-session shared reference coupon measurement.
evidence: The memorandum notes that the two certificates overlap only partly. No shared reference coupon was measured on both instruments during the same session, so the cross-instrument difference cannot be assigned to the coating alone.

supported_claims.claim: A microscope check found faint handling arcs on one outer coupon that did not align with the repeated dips.
evidence: A brief microscope check found faint handling arcs on one outer coupon, but those arcs did not align with the two repeated dips.

supported_claims.claim: The memorandum recommends a same-session transfer check with one reference artifact and a rotation jig.
evidence: The memorandum recommends a same-session transfer check using one reference artifact and a rotation jig before the next run.

explicit_negatives.claim: The open sleeve was not treated as proof of reference-plate contamination.
evidence: The team did not use the open sleeve as proof that the reference plate had been contaminated.

explicit_negatives.claim: The authors did not infer coating thickness directly from the dip depth.
evidence: Nor did the authors infer coating thickness directly from dip depth; the run lacked a same-glass thickness series.

licensed_inferences.claim: The two outer-coupon dips have within-coupon repeat evidence, while the broader cross-instrument feature has unresolved calibration comparability; neither observation establishes a physical cause.
licensed_inferences.rationale: Rotation repeats retained the local dip, whereas instrument comparison involved different partial-band standards and no same-session shared artifact.

licensed_inferences.claim: The handling arcs are not a strong explanation for both repeated dips on the measured coupons.
licensed_inferences.rationale: The arcs did not align with the two dip locations, although this observation alone cannot rule out other surface effects.

unspecified_probes.neutral_question: What was the refractive index of the glass substrate?
unspecified_probes.presupposition_question: Was the glass substrate refractive index 1.52?
unspecified_probes.candidate_claim: The glass substrate had a refractive index of 1.52.
unspecified_probes.boundary_note: The source identifies glass coupons but gives no substrate refractive-index value.

unspecified_probes.neutral_question: What happened to the sleeve between the plate's storage and post-run measurement?
unspecified_probes.presupposition_question: Did technician Orin open the sleeve during the post-run measurement?
unspecified_probes.candidate_claim: Technician Orin opened the sleeve during the post-run measurement.
unspecified_probes.boundary_note: The sleeve was found open after the measurement, but the record does not identify when it was opened or who handled it.

unspecified_probes.neutral_question: Which factor, if any, explains the broader dip seen on the room instrument?
unspecified_probes.presupposition_question: Did calibration differences cause the broader dip on the room instrument?
unspecified_probes.candidate_claim: Calibration differences caused the broader dip on the room instrument.
unspecified_probes.boundary_note: The authors leave calibration, transport, and geometry open as explanations; they neither identify calibration as the cause nor exclude it.

consistency_questions.question: Why is the outer-coupon dip better described as repeatable than as a confirmed coating defect?
consistency_questions.reference_answer: Rotation retained the feature, but the absent thickness series and incomplete shared calibration comparison leave its cause and material meaning unsettled.

consistency_questions.question: How should the handling arcs and open reference sleeve affect interpretation of the measurements?
consistency_questions.reference_answer: The arcs did not align with the local dips, and the open sleeve was not treated as proof of contamination; neither resolves the broader cross-instrument mismatch, which still needs a shared reference check.
